cases.narrative: At 3:45 p.m. on May 4, 2015, an employee was installing drainage pipes when thetrench collapsed. The employee was buried and died from asphyxiation.

At 9:00 a.m. on May 26, 2015, an employee was trouble a shooting elevatorequipment. The elevator car unexpectedly travelled downward, crushing theemployee between the elevator car and the steel structure. The employeesustained a crushed chest and head.

At 8:00 a.m. on July 31, 2015, an employee was working on an excavation. Theemployee looked into the excavation when it collapsed and engulfed him when a 10inch water main broke and he was covered with a water and mud mixture. Theemployee drowned as a result.

At 3:00 p.m. on October 19, 2015, an employee was standing on a four foot stepladder attempting to cut 1.5 inches off the top of a wood stud exterior wallwith a circular saw. The employee either fell off the four foot step ladder andmade contact with his inner leg with the saw or he brought the saw down from anoverhead raised position to rest his arms, and struck his inner leg. Theemployee was killed from a severe laceration to his femoral artery, and lost asignificant amount of blood before medical treatment could be provided.

At 3:00 p.m. on November 10, 2015, Employee #1, the owner of an excavationcompany, was engaged in excavation work at the site of new storage buildings. He was installing new sewer lines and connecting them to existing sewer lines. Earlier he had been working with his father, but at this time he was alone. Heentered a trench that was approximately 8 feet deep. The trench collapsed, andsoil, gravel, and a concrete slab fell onto Employee #1. He was fatallycrushed. The subsequent investigation determined Employee #1 had sustainedmultiple blunt force injuries to the area of his abdomen/diaphragm.

At 4:15 p.m. on November 13, 2015, Employee #1, employed by a trenching company, was installing sewer pipelines. He was working inside a 21-foot 6-inch trenchwhen a trench wall collapsed. Employee #1 was struck and buried under thefalling soil. Employee #1 was killed in the collapse.

At 1:00 p.m. on October 21, 2016, Employee #1 and #2 were preparing a trench forinstallation of a new sanitary sewer line. Both Employees were working at adepth of 11 feet and 11inches 2 events occurred, the straight cut walls of thetrench caved in and a fire hydrant came loose from the water main from which itwas attached. Soil covered Employees #1 and #2 and both were killed due toengulfment.

At 11:30 a.m. on December 15, 2016, an employee entered a trench and itcollapsed. While digging to find a sewer stub, a backhoe struck a sewer line. The employee climbed into the unprotected trench to investigate, the trenchcollapsed. The employee suffered asphyxia while being crushed by the dirt.

At approximately 4:00 p.m. on March 23, 2017, Employee #1, a carpenter, was drilling 0.25-inch holes in a precast concrete ceiling panel working from a 10 foot high step ladder. He was found on the floor with the ladder on top of him, dead.

At 3:30 p.m. on July 27, 2017, an employee was moving a work truck basket andcaught his head between the basket and a horizontal steel beam of an overheadawning. The employee sustained skull fractures, lacerations, contusions andwas killed.

At 10:09 a.m. on October 16, 2017, an employee was spotting the operator of the trencher. The employee got caught in the rotating chain drive of the trencher and was killed from multiple cuts and lacerations.

At 10:30 a.m. on March 8, 2018, Employee #1 was shimming a piece of 2 inch by 4 inch lumber underneath a rack stand while a coworker was hitting a stand, loaded by a rebar cage, with a sledgehammer. The rebar cage shifted, causing the rack stand to fall over and trap Employee #1 between the rebar cage and the horizontal beam of the rack stand. Employee #1’s torso was crushed, resulting in his death.

At 4:00 p.m. on March 25, 2018, an employee was retracting the outrigger of thePalfinger Crane, Model PK 50002 EH, and was pinned against the control panel andthe stabilizer of the outrigger, crushing his chest, abdomen, and pelvic area. The employee was killed.

At 9:30 a.m. on June 14, 2018, Employee #1 was tying in a 0.75 inch copperpiping in the main water line, standing approximately eight feet deep in atrench. The employee was working on his knees when the trench collapsed andburied the employee. Employee #1 suffered major head trauma and later died dueto an excessive loss of blood.

At 3:00 p.m. on July 23, 2019, Employees #1 and #2, employed by a drainage services company, were working in a trench at the site of a residential structure. The trench sidewall collapsed, and the two employees were buried under approximately 2 feet of soil. Employees #1 and #2 were killed, cause of death asphyxiation.

At 3:30 a.m. on September 17, 2019, an employee was working as a crane oiler ata construction site. The employee was caught between the crane tracks and thecrane’s counter weight and crushed. The employee was killed by the unspecifiedcrush injuries received.

At 3:00 p.m. on July 23, 2019, Employee #1 and Employee # 2 were working in atrench to expose a drainage pipe for removal. The sidewall of the trenchcollapsed, burying the employees under approximately 2 feet of soil. Employee #1and Employee #2 were both killed due to asphyxiation.

At 11:30 a.m. on April 27, 2020, Employee #1 and a coworker, employed by aconstruction company, were engaged in a sewer pipeline installation for a newcommercial construction project. Employee #1 was in the excavation andattempting to connect PVC pipe to the steel connector of the horizontal drillsystem. His coworker was operating the drilling equipment. During thisactivity, the PVC pipe began to rotate violently. Employee #1 was caughtbetween the PVC pipe and the trench box. Emergency services transportedEmployee #1 to the hospital, where he received treatment for abdominal injuries. The employee died from his injuries.

At 12:30 a.m. on June 2, 2020, an employee was standing in a concrete materialplacing machine hopper while cleaning it while the hopper auger was rotating andcaught the employee by the legs and amputated them. The amputation injurieskilled the employee.

At 9:15 a.m. on August 28, 2020, an employee was working to separate aprefabricated wall to push it square. The employee used a concrete plunge saw tocut it apart when the saw kicked back and struck the employee’s throat. Theemployee received a severe throat laceration and was killed.

At 2:30 p.m. on October 27, 2020, Employee #1, Coworkers #1 and #2, and theirsupervisor, divers employed by a civil engineering construction company, wereengaged in a diving operation at a lake dam. They were assigned to conductinspections and repairs to several gates and chains. During a solitary divewith an umbilical supplying breathing gas and video, Employee #1 climbed down along ladder to the water’s surface. He then descended into the water, slidingdown the chain with his right hand while feeling the side of the dam face withhis left hand to guide his way down. At a depth of approximately 15 to 20 feet, his left hand came into contact with a 10-inch hole in the dam’s face that ledinto a Penstock Pipe. Differential pressure caused the employee’s left arm tobe sucked into the pipe up to his shoulder. He cried out and then went silentand unresponsive. The dive supervisor attempted several times to communicatewith Employee #1 but received no response. The supervisor instructed Coworker#1, the backup diver, to go into the water. Coworker #1, after reachingEmployee #1, reported that Employee #1 remained unresponsive with no signs ofbreathing. Coworker #1 was unable to free him from the pipe. Several damemployees were called to the scene, and one of the dam operators closed a valvewhich released the diver from the pipe. Coworker #1 brought Employee #1 to thewater’s surface, where he was attached to the emergency retrieval system, removed from the water, and placed on the main deck where emergency medicaltechnicians were standing by. Employee #1 was transported to the hospital, where he was declared dead. The subsequent investigation reported thatmechanical asphyxiation may have been the cause of death. At no time hadEmployee #1 lost air.

At 8:30 a.m. on December 9, 2020, Employees #1, #2, and #3, employed by ademolition company, were performing demolition work at a power generationfacility. The work was in preparation for the implosion of a boiler room andportions of the control room. The building structure collapsed onto the threeemployees. Employees #1 and #2 were transported to the hospital, where theywere admitted for treatment of multiple injuries. Employee #3’s body was foundand recovered later. He had been killed in the collapse.

At 4:00 p.m. on December 21, 2020, Employee #1 and coworkers, employed by awater and sewer line construction company, were attempting to repair aresidential sewer line that was back flowing. While they were in the trenchthey had dug, a trench wall collapsed. Employee #1 was caught in the collapsingmaterial and fatally crushed.

At 5:30 p.m. on April 28, 2021, an employee operated a Komatsu Excavator with asheer attachment to demolish a coal silo. At some point, the employee exited theexcavator to pull a piece of metal from the structure when the silo collapsedonto and killed the employee.

At 9:00 a.m. on May 28, 2021, an employee used a hammer to remove the four pinsthat held the mid-section of a crane boom together. When the employee removedthe third pin, the crane boom section fell on top of the employee, who waskilled by crush injuries.
At 12:36 p.m. on May 4, 2021, an employee worked to expose a pipe on thesidewall of the trench. At some point, the trench collapsed onto the employee, who was asphyxiated and killed.

At 2:30 a.m. on July 26, 2022, an employee was climbing into a trench. Theemployee climbed onto the end of the trench box (spreader bars), and one side ofthe two point sling came unhooked from the trench box, causing the box to falland pin the employee between the spreader bars and wall of the trench. Theemployee was killed due to a crushed chest and head.

At 10:30 a.m. on November 19, 2022, an employee was cleaning debris on thebottom level of the work area when a coworker began descending the stairwellfrom the second level and it collapsed. The employee was crushed underneath thestairwell and died from his injuries.

On March 11, 2023, an employee working for a roads and bridges constructioncompany was attempting to dump a load of dirt onto a stockpile. The truck bedwould not fully extend and got stuck. The employee climbed under the truck bedand attempted to troubleshoot the problem. Then, he climbed on top of the frameof the truck. The hydraulics gave out and the bed collapsed crushing theemployee’s head and body, killing him.
At 3:45 p.m. on September 6, 2023, an employee was working on a soil screenermachine. The employee’s head was crushed by the conveyor section of the soilscreener machine. The employee was killed.

At 7:30 a.m. on April 13, 2015, an employee was relocating an alternate powerdistribution loop for the main mall power system. The employee locked andtagged out the circuit and, proceeded to a junction box to cut the 7.2V powercables. However, when the employee cut into the cable, he cut into an energizedcable of the wrong power distribution loop. The employee was electrocuted anddied two days later.
At 5:00 p.m. on May 16, 2015, an employee was operating an aerial lift, contacted overhead power lines, and was electrocuted to death.
At 3:21 p.m. on May 13, 2015, an employee was walking across a roof whenlightning struck a direct hit. The employee suffered fatal burns to head andwas electrocuted.

On June 17, 2015, Employee #1, part of a five man crew, was installingunderground storm sewer connections for buildings downspouts. A coworker, operating a John Deere Model 50 mini excavator, was creating a 4 foot excavationto lay piping. The excavator bucket contacted a plastic underground conduit withfive conductors within totaling 480 volts. The coworker called out to everyoneto back away and not touch the exposed live conductors as did the foreman. Employee #1 bent down and his right hand came in contact with the installationand was exposed to 277 volts on a 60 ampere circuit. The excavation was 29inches deep and the damaged conduit was 1.5 inch inside diameter. Employee #1was electrocuted.

At 10:15 p.m. on January 21, 2105, an employee was carrying a piece of aluminumflashing up a ladder. The victim lost control of the flashing in the windyconditions. The flashing contacted the adjacent energized power line. Thevictim was electrically shocked which caused him to fall approximately 18 feetfrom the ladder. Employee succumbed to injuries and died.

At approximately 11:30 a.m. on September 1, 2015, an employee was removing 12-2metal clad (MC) wire from a 2-ft by 4-ft recessed light. The employee turned offthe wrong 20 amp circuit breaker at the panel. The circuit was connected to afour way light switch. The employee assumed the circuit was de-energizedbecause it did not test positive for an electric current. An unknown person inanother part of the facility turned on the light at a different location whichenergized the 277 volt/20 amp circuits. The employee received electric shockfrom an energized, 277 volt /20amp, recessed lighting circuit and was killed.circuit and was killed.

At approximately 11:47 a.m. on September 22, 2015, an employee was installing alight fixture in the women rest room. The employee was working with a wire thathe believed was not hot. However, the wires were crossed. At some point, theemployee made contact with the wire and was electrocuted.
At 10:30 a.m. on July 9, 2015, an employee was changing a light bulb in aswimming pool. The employee was electrocuted when they contacted a live circuitthat was supposed to be off.
At 8:15 a.m. on April 7, 2016, an employee was killed from an electrical burn.
At approximately 12:00 a.m. on July 24, 2016, Employee #1 was servicing a coiland condenser in a residential attic. He was found unconscious and died fromelectrocution.

At 10:48 p.m. on November 22, 2016, an employee was installing rain gutters. The ladder the employee was using came into contact with electrical power lines, and the employees was electrocuted and died.
At approximately 6:30 p.m. on March 16, 2017, Employee #1 was electrocuted.

At 2:00 p.m. on August 11, 2017, Employee # 1 and Employee #2 were workingoutside of a single family residence with a Marathon Electric Vacuum Pump, Model#80L48C17D4708P, Serial # 1201. Employee #1 was working with a 16-3 extensioncord that was plugged into a three-pronged receptacle located in an enclosedpatio area of a house that was damp. Employee #1 received a shock from a vacuumpump and was electrocuted. Employee #2 received an electrical shock whentouching Employee #1 who was lying on the ground in an unresponsive state.state.

At 2:30 a.m. on May 3, 2018, Employee #1 was attempting to fix a 3 phase14,000/24976 downed power line. As the employee spliced the two lines together, the lines became energized and the employee was electrocuted.
At 8:30 a.m. on May 23, 2018, an employee was installing a flexible all-weatherelectrical conduit when he was electrocuted.

At 9:30 a.m. on July 20, 2019, an employee was operating a Skytrax telehandlertraveling to a staging area to pick up roofing materials. The boom was in theelevated position and made contact with an energized 69kv power line. Theemployee was electrocuted.
At 8:25 a.m. on October 5, 2018, an employee was installing a ground line for awork table and touched a live circuit, electrocuting himself.

At 2:00 p.m. on June 7, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a signs company, wasrepairing a business’s roadside sign and replacing the lighting inside the sign. The employer became concerned that Employee #1’s vehicle, installed with a GPSsystem, had shown no sign of movement for two hours. The employer called thebusiness and asked that Employee #1 be checked on. The business’s operationsmanager went out to the sign and discovered Employee #1 lying unresponsiveinside the sign. Emergency services were called, and Employee #1’s body wasrecovered. He had been killed by electrocution while working on the sign’slighting.
At 3:13 p.m. on July 8, 2019, Employee #1, employed by an air conditioning andheating services company, was welding a coopering pipe to an air conditioningunit at a job site. He was electrocuted.

At 11:00 a.m. on October 1, 2019, an employee was directing the flow of concretewhile pouring a new foundation using a pump hose. While pouring the concrete, acoworker operating the boom pump, made contact with a 13kv overhead electricalline. When contact was made the employee was killed by electrocution due to thevoltage passing though the pump hose he was holding.
At 2:00 p.m. on April 20, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company, was engaged in a power line installation. The employee was electrocuted.electrocuted.

At 11:00 a.m. on August 30, 2021, an employee worked to paint a metaltransmission tower. The employee worked in a section with live, high voltagepower lines. The employee made contact with the power lines, was electrocuted, and killed.

At 11:45 a.m. on December 13, 2021, an employee installed corner flashing on abuilding. As the employee repositioned the aluminum ladder, the ladder contactedan overhead power line. The employee was killed by electrocution.

At 5:30 p.m. on October 14, 2022, an employee took his lunch break and returnedto his office and at some point made contact with an energized lighting systemcomponent. The employee was found on the floor of his office unresponsive anddied due to electrocution.
At 1:59 p.m. on February 7, 2023, an employee was installing metal roofing. Theemployee was moving with a piece of metal roofing and hit a high voltagepowerline. The employee was electrocuted.
At 2:00 p.m. on July 24, 2023, an employee working as a roofer for a roofingcontractor was sitting under a tree. The employee was struck by lightning andkilled due to electrocution.

At 9:30 a.m. on August 23, 2023, an employee was setting up a crane for thefirst lift of the project. The crane rigging made contact with the overhead13,200-volt power lines. The employee sustained fatal electrical burns and waselectrocuted.

At 3:00 a.m. on November 8, 2023, Employee #1 was working for a framingcontractor. Employee #1 was hanging Christmas Lights on an evergreen tree at aresidential address. Employee #1 was using a fiberglass pole to hang Christmaslights on an evergreen tree in the backyard of a residential home. Thefiberglass pole and/or Christmas lights contacted the energized 69KV power lineand the employee was electrocuted. Employee #1 also suffered 3rd degree burns.

At 1:00 p.m. on June 24, 2024, Employee #1, employed as a maintenancetechnician, was working on an outside air unit when he came into contact with anelectrical source. The employee was electrocuted, sustaining fatal injuries fromthe electrical contact. Emergency services responded to the scene, but theemployee was pronounced dead from the electrocution.

At 3:30 p.m. on December 30, 2024, Employee #1 was working under an 18-foot tallplatform installing a dryer vent when he began spasming and called for help. Coworkers pulled him out and found blood in his mouth. He was transported to thehospital but was pronounced dead about an hour later. The cause of injury waselectrocution from electricity associated with the dryer.
At 8:30 p.m. on January 14, 2016, an employee was performing saw cutting onconcrete/demolition. The employee was on break when he fell into the river. Theemployee drowned.

At 10:30 a.m. on February 26, 2016, an employee climbing an extension ladder toframe around a wood stove "B" vent on a roof, fell from the top of the 23-footladder to the ground. He sustained head trauma and was killed.

At 1:50 p.m. on November 3, 2016, an employee was dragging plywood from unit 1to unit 3 where they were decking. The employee fell 22 feet through anunguarded stairwell opening onto the first level of a concrete floor. Theemployee sustained head trauma and was killed.
At 2:30 p.m. on June 13, 2017, an employee fell from a scaffold while painting. He suffered a concussion and died as a result.

At 5:56 p.m. on September 5, 2017, an employee was tearing off old shingles froma residential structure. The employee was installing some metal flashing in aroof valley and slipped on a wet surface. The employee fell 17 feet from an8-10/12 pitch roof to the ground alongside the driveway. The employee wastransported to the local hospital where he was pronounced dead by the ER doctor.doctor.
At 2:00 p.m. on February 15, 2018, an employee was walking to one side of theroof to another when he fell and struck the pavement below, killing him.

At 3:00 a.m. on April 20, 2018, an employee was blowing insulation in an atticof a single family residential home and fell through the ceiling after receivingan electrical shock from an energized television antenna that did not have aground wire. The employee fell approximately 8 feet to the house floor and waskilled.
At 12:15 p.m. on June 11, 2018, an employee was walking on the top of a buss duct or other electrical equipment. The employee fell 14 feet to the floor, sustained a head injury, and died.

At 8:30 a.m. on September 4, 2018, an employee was preparing the roof for theremoval of old roof shingles and stepped through a skylight opening that wasremoved the previous week. The employee fell 23 feet and was killed from bluntforce head trauma when he struck the concrete floor.

At 1:00 p.m. on October 10, 2018, an employee was gluing and securing EPDMrubber sheathing on the roof. The employee stepped into an unguarded hole in theroof and fell approximately 22 feet and struck a 2 x 6, a metal pipe, and ametal storage rack before landing on the concrete floor. The employee sufferedmultiple injuries to include a fractured femur and spine along with massive headtrauma. The employee was killed.
At 11:45 a.m. on October 14, 2018, an employee was cleaning up some debris on aroof and fell through an unguarded skylight to the concrete floor, killing him.
At 5:32 p.m. on January 31, 2019, an employee was climbing a ladder and fell, fracturing her arm when she landed on the floor.

At 3:15 p.m. on August 15, 2018, an employee was installing rubber roofingmembrane. He was rolling it out and walking backwards. The employee, accordingto the supervisor, tripped and fell through the open hole in the roof, theunguarded/uncovered skylight. The employee died on August 27, 2018 due torespiratory failure due to pneumonia complicated by blunt force trauma to headwith fractures of skull, cerebral contusions, and subarachnoid hemorrhage.hemorrhage.

At 7:30 a.m. on July 31, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a home builder, was working at the site of a new two-story residential structure. He was installing .75 inch plywood decking to second-story structural beams. Employee #1 fell, a fall height of approximately 20 feet, and struck the basement’s concrete floor. Emergency services transported Employee #1 to the hospital, where he died from injuries sustained in the fall.

At 3:45 p.m. on July 18, 2019, Employee #1, employed by a concrete company, was working at the site of a new two-story multifamily residential building. He was standing on a 6-foot ladder when he fell. Employee #1 sustained fatal head and chest injuries.

At 9:50 a.m. on June 15, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a roofing company, wasworking at a multi-employer construction project, a two-story multifamilyresidential structure that required repairs. He was using a 28-foot aluminumLouisville extension ladder, Type II, to access the roof so he could develop anestimate of roofing repair costs. The employee fell from the ladder, a fallheight of 13 feet. A coworker saw him on the ground and found him unresponsive. Emergency services transported the employee to the hospital, where he waspronounced dead. The Medical Examiner determined the cause of death was bluntforce trauma to the neck.

At 10:00 a.m. on September 28, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a paintingcontractor, was working at a one-story residential structure. He was standingon a ladder and applying caulk when he lost balance, fell, and struck his headagainst the brick patio, a fall height of 18 feet. Employee #1 was killed. Investigation revealed the employee was using the wrong equipment and, to reachthe area being caulked, had to over extend his body away from the ladder when helost balance and fell.

At 11:30 a.m. on November 2, 2020, Employees #1 and #2, employed by acommunications installation and repair company, were hanging a 5G antenna on awater tower. They were working from the basket of an aerial lift when the liftfell over, likely due to high winds. The two employees and the lift fell 125feet, and the lift landed on the employees. Both employees were killed.

At 12:46 p.m. on March 31, 2021, an employee worked to install exterior andtruss wood framing. At some point, the employee fell approximately forty feetand received multiple blunt force trauma injuries to the torso and internalorgans and was killed.
At 5:15 p.m. on July 28, 2021, an employee installed shingles on a roof. At somepoint, the employee fell approximately twenty feet and was killed due to a headinjury.

At 11:15 a.m. on October 28, 2021, an employee worked to remove underlayment ona residential roof. While pulling up a section, it pulled up easier thanexpected, the employee lost balance and fell approximately seventeen feet. Theemployee received a skull fracture and was killed.

At 8:00 a.m. on April 22, 2022, an employee, a roofer, was working on acommercial building roof. The employee tripped and fell 5 stories to the groundand broke his right femur fractured his skull. The employee died as a result ofhis injuries.

At 10:00 a.m. on August 15, 2022, an employee was standing on the platform of aBaker’s scaffold installing tracks along the wall for metal studs. The wheels onthe scaffold were not locked. The employee, while standing on the platform, tried to scoot the scaffold. The employee fell off the scaffold and hit theconcrete floor 6 feet below. In the fall, he brought the scaffold down on top ofhim. The employee incurred head/skull injuries and broken ribs and was killed.

At 9:00 a.m. on November 3, 2022, an employee was performing exterior framingcarpentry on the roof of a new multifamily residential construction project. Theemployee fell 31 feet off the roof of the three story building. The employee waskilled by blunt force injuries, lacerations and fractures.

At 9:45 a.m. on June 20, 2023, an employee was standing on a section of the roofwith a 4/12 pitch and placing metal flashing in the transition portion of theroof above the entrance of the cabin. The employee slipped while working and theforce of his legs swinging off and below the roof line caused him to flingbackward. The employee hit a stair railing below the area he was working andstruck his upper back/lower neck on the railing, causing his death. The employeesuffered a hemorrhage/internal bleeding to the brain.

At 11:24 a.m. on May 27, 2023, an employee was descending a ladder and slipped. The employee lost his balance and fell striking a propane grill and the ground. The employee sustained head trauma and died three days later.

At 2:30 p.m. on July 12, 2023, an employee working as a journeyman plumber on acrew for a plumbing contractor had entered a manhole. The employee needed tounclog a sewage line that he and his crew were installing. The employee stood onthe second step down into the manhole and attempted to reach the line openingwhen he lost his footing. He fell approximately 20 feet to the bottom. Theemployee sustained internal organ damage and died.

At 2:52 p.m. on March 20, 2024, an employee was spray painting a wood gable. The employee stepped onto an unsecured 2x4 on the roof and slipped and fell off. The employee suffered broken bones and internal injuries and was killed.

At approximately 9:30 a.m. on July 3, 2024, Employee #1 was working to secure atarp over soil on the back of a Ford F-350 dump truck. While pulling the tarp, the employee may have lost his grip and slipped, falling from the truck onto thepavement below. The employee struck his head on the pavement, sustaining fatalinjuries. Emergency services were contacted, but the employee was pronounceddead at the scene.

At 4:00 p.m. on August 12, 2024, Employee #1 was leaving the roof to return tothe floor at the end of the workday when he fell from a scissor lift to theconcrete. The employee sustained multiple injuries from the fall. Emergencyresponders were called to the scene, but the employee was pronounced dead fromthe injuries sustained upon impact with the concrete floor.

At 6:44 p.m. on January 29, 2015, two employees were carrying a piece of achicken rack (leg) to a staging area. The legs were being set on their edge andleaned against the inside of an exterior wall of the building that the employeeswere working in. The employees set the leg down on the ground against a stackof legs that had already been set down and stacked. As the employees set theleg onto the existing stack, the stack began to fall away from the wall. Theemployee began to back out of the way of the falling stack of legs. As theemployee was backing out of the way, he tripped and fell to the floor, strikinghis head on the platform of an aerial lift that was parked nearby. The employeeshead struck the steel platform of an aerial lift where he suffered a major headinjury and died.
At 11:00 a.m. on May 4, 2015, an employee carried metal studs into worksite. Theemployee tripped or collapsed and struck head against a rock wall. The employeewas found non-responsive and later died.

At 7:30 p.m. on February 25, 2016, an employee who just arrived at the worksitewas exiting a truck, slipped on ice, and struck his head on the asphalt parkinglot. Following the incident, the employee told co-workers about the incidentand said did not feel well. The employee was admitted to the hospital, developed a coma, and died March 15, 2016, from blunt force trauma to the head.trauma to the head.

At 5:00 p.m. on September 7, 2016, an employee was taking a break, walking to orfrom the bathroom. The employee fainted and fell backwards, he hit his head onthe floor and was killed from a head laceration.

At 11:00 a.m. on October 5, 2016, an employee was planning some conduit routingwhen he tripped over an unprotected edge and fell to the floor, striking hishead as he fell. The employee had a head injury and multiple body injuries.body injuries.

On April 3, 2017, an employee fell to the ground while walking. He was impaledby a screwdriver resulting in puncture of aorta. The employee was taken to thePresbyterian hospital where he died the following day.

At 10:00 a.m. on February 8, 2018, an employee had loaded a furnace in the backof a truck before falling backwards and striking his head onto the concretesurface. The employee was killed as a result of his injuries.

At 2:00 p.m. on March 7, 2018, per the employee’s wife, the employee wasretrieving tools/equipment from a work van when he lost his footing and fellbackwards. He hit his head; however, did not report the incident. When he washospitalized an approximate month later for a hematoma to his head, the employeedied.

At 3:00 p.m. on August 21, 2018, an employee was using guide lines while afiberglass pool was being unloaded from a delivery trailer. The employee jumpedonto the trailer and started to push against the pools to speed up the unloadingand lost his balance, falling against the jagged edge of the top pool. Theemployee cut his face and lacerated the main arteries in his neck, killing him.killing him.

At 12:00 p.m. on June 25, 2020, Employee #1, employed by a construction company, was engaged in form work for a new road. He was using a sledge hammer to set aform stake for a footing. The employee missed the stake, and the weight of thehammer caused the employee to twist and fall on his right knee. The employeewas transported to the hospital and treated for a sprained right knee and a tornmedial meniscus. The employee required amputation above the right knee. Aninfection developed, and Employee #1 died from complications of the originalinjury.

At 8:30 a.m. on January 28, 2020, an employee parked a trailer. While walking ona skid steer, the employee tripped, fell, and received a liver laceration. Theemployee was hospitalized to treat the injury, but later died.
