An employee was working on a roof while installing a membrane roofing system over an existing metal roof. The employee was pulling a generator cord out of the way when he fell off the roof edge approximately 20 feet into muddy ground, resulting in a fractured pelvis and right lung contusion.

The injured employee was standing on a precast plank. A weld was cut from the plank causing it and the injured employee to fall about 10 feet to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured hip.
A masonry worker was on a scaffold when a 2-by-4 broke, causing the employee to fall to the ground and suffer two broken arms.
An employee was on a roof applying shingles. The employee fell from the roof, suffering a head laceration and a broken leg.
An employee was working on an 8-foot step ladder when they fell off the ladder, resulting in broken ribs and a broken shoulder.
An employee was cleaning windows from a ladder. He fell off the ladder and suffered a broken hip. He was hospitalized.
An employee was on a ladder hanging a gutter when the ladder slipped and the employee fell. They sustained a fractured right hip and a head laceration.

An employee was spotting for materials that were being raised to a platform. The employee was moving a box out of the way on the platform when they fell 12 feet to the concrete below. They sustained contusions and rib fractures.

An employee was on a 10-foot ladder, hanging LED tape lighting on faux wooden beams. The beams fell from the ceiling and knocked the employee from the ladder to the floor. He sustained a fractured back.

An employee was installing asphalt roofing when the wooden beam they were tied to gave way. They fell 10 feet to the ground and landed on their bottom. The employee sustained fractures to their lower back.
While working on the roof of a new commercial building, an employee tripped and fell, landing on a steel purlin. The employee lacerated the left arm and required surgery and hospitalization.

An employee was employed as a tour guide for this steel mill facility. He was giving a tour and was walking down a two step set of stairs when he missed the second step and fell to the floor. Later that day he went to the hospital and was admitted for three broken ribs on his left side.
An employee was walking across a concrete area covered by black ice and snow. The employee slipped and fell, sustaining two fractures to the left ankle and requiring hospitalization.
A employee slipped and fell on ice, fracturing his right femur and requiring surgery.

An employee was moving a pipe to another pipe to be welded. As the employee was maneuvering out of the way of the moving pipe, he tripped on another pipe that was laying on the ground. He fell onto that pipe and broke his left wrist, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was canting a pole (moving a power pole from the ground to a standing position) when the rope and cant hook slipped because they were wet. The employee fell backwards and put his hands behind him to catch himself. He landed on his right hand and broke it near the wrist.
While unloading supplies from a truck, an employee slipped on ice and broke an ankle.
An employee fell down the stairs and suffered head trauma, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was picking up a roll of rubber in the storage shed and lost his footing. He fell on the 4" storage lip and broke his hip.
An employee was stepping off a tractor, missed the last step and fell onto their hip breaking it. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee tripped and fell to the floor inside an elevator, injuring both shoulders.

Three employees were walking down the stairs. The stairs collapsed and two of the employees were injured. They suffered multiple fractures, contusions, and lacerations to the legs, arms, ankles, back and chest.
An employee slipped and fell on an icy walkway while entering a job site. He fell to the ground, suffering a leg fracture that required surgery.
An employee was attempting to straighten a digging bar that was wedged in a backhoe. When the bar moved, the employee lost balance and fell breaking the left ankle.

An employee was on the ground spreading dirt/gravel with a metal concrete rake when they slipped on loose dirt and fell onto the rake. The employee suffered a rib fracture and a contusion on the spleen.
The injured employee was moving a stone up one level to another employee on a scaffold, when he lost his balance and fell on the stone he was standing on, injuring his back and hand.

An employee was attempting to punch a hole into the cooling tower support beam using the hydraulic punch set. The employee’s foot slipped out on uneven ground and the employee fell to the ground dropping the tool onto his leg and fracturing it.
An employee tripped and fell while walking. The employee struck a rock on the ground and sustained a possible fractured femur.
An employee was walking between a trailer and a truck. He tripped and fell, and a diesel gas can he had been holding cut three fingers on his right hand.

An employee was walking through a basement when he became entangled in a pull wire on the floor, causing him to fall onto the concrete floor. The employee was hospitalized for a fractured left elbow that required surgery.
An employee was placing plastic over duct work when they tripped and landed on the duct work. The metal duct work lacerated the employee’s forearm.
An employee was opening a gate when they tripped on a curb and fell to the concrete ground, resulting in an open head wound and a broken rib.
An employee was walking, slipped on wet slurry, fell, and broke his femur.

An employee was walking to pick up materials when he slipped and fell onto a wooden board. He suffered a puncture wound to the right side of his head, caused by a nail that was sticking out of the board.
An employee was on a rooftop, screwing down a bolt with a wrench. The wrench slipped. He lost his balance and fell onto the screw, which lacerated the inside of his right hand. He was hospitalized.
An employee was pulling on a pry bar to put rebar into the correct spacing. The employee tripped and suffered a dislocated and fractured right ankle.
An employee was working from a platform on a concrete curbing machine. The employee stepped onto another platform, slipped, and fell on the platform, suffering a broken right tibia.
An employee was walking from a break area to a work station. The employee tripped over a rod and fell to the floor, suffering an arm injury. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was backing up a dump truck when it got stuck. He got out of the vehicle and was moving to the rear when he lost his balance on the uneven ground and fell. He suffered a torn muscle in the left leg.

An employee was walking in the onsite parking garage when they slipped on ice and fell on their back, hip, and head. The employee sustained a headache and internal bleeding that caused a seizure. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was hit by the blast of a sand blaster, which injected media into his leg.

An employee was grinding on an auxiliary diesel fuel tank to fix a clog when a spark from the grinding wheel ignited diesel fumes inside the tank and it exploded. A piece of the exploding tank hit and broke his right leg below the knee, requiring surgery.

Two employees were switching circuits in a circuit breaker when an arc flash/blast occurred. They were running from the blast when an oil-filled transformer exploded burning the employees. One of the employees was hospitalized due to the burns.

An employee was cutting the bolt heads off carrier flights of conveyor chain when the oxygen hose on the torch unit sprung a leak and the oxygen ignited. The employee’s shirt caught on fire and the employee was burned on the left side of his chest.

An employee was standing on a 6-foot ladder making repairs to an approximately 25’ tall x 10’ wide x 15’ deep air rotation unit when an explosion occurred and knocked him from the ladder. Flames erupted from the unit, causing third degree burns to his face. He was hospitalized.
An employee was welding tube steel above his head when a spark entered his coat and caught it on fire. He received second and third degree burns to his left arm from his elbow to his fingers.

An employee was working on an electrical component of the water pump when the lead contacts sparked. The sparks ignited an unknown gas that was coming from a capped well in the work area. The employee was engulfed in flames and sustained first and second degree burns to both hands and wrists and first degree burns to his face.

The injured employee was applying flammable, solvent-based adhesive on the roof. As he walked by another employee using a torch to dry the roof, the employee’s clothes ignited. The injured employee then entered the area where the adhesive was being applied and a fire started. The injured employee sustained burns to about 80 percent of his body and was hospitalized.
An employee was refueling a gas-powered air compressor. Fuel contacted the hot muffler and ignited. The employee suffered burns to the hands, face and chest.
An employee’s left ring finger was amputated after a pressurized airline ruptured in his hand.

An employee was operating a trenching machine when it struck an old, unmarked natural gas pipeline. The machine caught fire before the operator could turn it off; he suffered burns to his right hand as he left the cab, as well as a broken right knee and left wrist as he jumped to the ground. He was hospitalized.

An employee was setting a pier column and needed to cut a piece of rebar with a gas-powered saw. When the employee started the saw to cut the rebar, it exploded and his pant leg caught on fire, burning the back of his left leg.

An employee was standing near a low-pressure separator. A flash fire in the separator caused a hose to become detached. The hose struck the employee in the head. Fire was coming out of the hose when it became detached and the employee was burned on the head as well. The employee was hospitalized for a head injury and burns.
An employee opened a trailer. A propane leak within the trailer caused an explosion and the employee suffered severe hand burns.
An employee was filling the pressure washer with gas. The tank slipped from his hand and fuel splashed onto his legs. The gas was ignited by the hot engine and one of the employee’s legs was burned.
An employee was taking the cap off a pressurized fire hydrant. The cap blew off and struck the employee in the right leg fracturing the tibia and fibula. The employee required surgery.
An employee was lighting a propane burner when a flash fire burned the employee’s hands and face.
An employee was using welding equipment. Residual solvent fumes ignited and the employee was hospitalized for burns.
An employee was performing blasting operations when his foot slipped. The blast nozzle contacted his abdominal and upper thigh area, and he suffered abrasions from the blast medium.

Employees were making emergency repairs to the girder of a bridge that was struck by a tractor-trailer. The injured employee was waiting for grinding to be completed so he could stick-weld. He was standing next to a hanging torch when a spark from the grinding caused leaking propane to ignite. The employee sustained a flash burn to his right ankle and required hospitalization.
An employee was filling a jockey pump with gasoline when some gas spilled on a hot muffler and ignited, burning the employee’s left ear, lips, left cheek, and right hand.

An employee was unclogging a steel pipe oil line with an air tank. The oil line fitting ruptured, causing the employee to sustain a laceration to the left forearm and right side of head. The fitting then sparked and created a flash fire. The employee sustained first-degree burns to the face and second-degree burns to both arms.

An employee was fueling a chop saw in preparation to cut rebar. After placing the saw in a horizontal position, the gas cap leaked fuel onto the employee’s leg. The sparks from cutting then ignited the fuel, causing the employee to sustain burns to the left leg and hands.
An employee was cutting steel with a torch when their jacket caught fire. The employee sustained burns to their arms and back.
An employee was burning a brush pile. They poured gasoline on the fire, resulting in burns to his face, arms, and hands.
Two employees were using gasoline and bar oil to ignite a brush pile when a flash fire occurred. An employee sustained burns to their face, arms, and hands.

On November 30, 2023, the injured employee was using a torch to melt ice and snow off a roof so another employee could apply a primer to seal a gutter to the roof. The 3-gallon bucket of primer ignited on the roof. The injured employee went to move the bucket off the roof when primer splashed onto him, causing him to catch on fire. The employee suffered third-degree burns.

An employee was cutting metal studs on the exterior framing. He used a chop saw blade on a grinder and the blade exploded, resulting in amputation of his left index finger. The grinder was unguarded at the time of the incident.
An employee was using fuel to light a brush pile when they sustained second-degree burns on their right arm.

An employee was using a torch to dismantle a boiler in the basement when the torch slipped out of his hand and swung in the opposite direction, catching his shirt on fire. The employee sustained a burn to his right arm and the right side of his stomach.

An employee was removing a hose from an asphalt truck. When the employee unhooked the hose, the oil remaining in the hose splashed back onto the employee’s left arm, causing chemical burns. He was hospitalized.
An employee was sandblasting structural steel. He was using supply air from an air compressor when he felt lightheaded. He was hospitalized for carbon monoxide exposure.
An employee was hospitalized with chemical burns during a concrete cutting operation.
An employee was pouring concrete when concrete entered his boots, causing a chemical burn that became infected.

An employee was performing demolition activities. The employee removed a ceiling tile and liquid from a water pipe spilled onto the employee. Shortly thereafter, the employee suffered lack of muscle control, nervous system depression, and memory loss. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was using a gas-powered pressure washer inside the basement of a residential construction site to wash out the concrete floor when he started to feel dizzy and was overcome by carbon monoxide poisoning. He was hospitalized.

An employee was disconnecting gauges from a condenser when a valve failed to close, releasing refrigerant from the system. The employee attempted to shut the valve with a wrench and was exposed to refrigerant, receiving a chemical burn to the right hand.
An employee was engaged in various electrical installation activities throughout the day. That evening he began to feel ill and was hospitalized for dehydration.

An employee was operating a bulldozer in a pond where hydrogen sulfide had been detected by monitoring devices. The employee was found unconscious and required hospitalization. Personal protective equipment was not worn at the time.
Two employees were cutting with a saw when carbon monoxide built up. They suffered carbon monoxide poisoning and were hospitalized.
While painting, an employee went to drink water out of a plastic bottle, but the bottle contained a chemical called xylene. The employee ingested the chemical and was hospitalized.
A chlorine spill occurred at the worksite and the chlorine fumes caused respiratory distress for two employees.
An employee sustained a fractured leg while trying to move a blast pot used in abrasive blasting.

Two employees were using a propane-powered saw indoors to cut concrete. They began to feel sick, stopped work, and went to the doorway for some fresh air. One of them lost consciousness and was hospitalized, suffering from carbon monoxide poisoning.

An employee was taking apart a flange to a 2-inch pipe. Alkaline product inside the pipe sprayed onto his forehead, upper chest, and abdomen. He suffered chemical burns in those areas, including third-degree burns to the chest and abdomen.
An employee was waiting in the cab of his truck to deliver materials to a worksite when he was overcome by what was believed to be carbon monoxide exposure.
A driver was exposed to carbon monoxide while waiting in his truck. He became ill and was hospitalized.
An employee was doing form work when concrete/cement got into his boots. He sustained chemical burns.
Two employees were pouring an acid mixture into a vat that contained bleach. A chemical reaction occurred and the mixture erupted onto the employees. Both employees were burned and hospitalized.
An employee was cleaning toilets at a rest stop and had trouble breathing due to the fumes produced from the mixture of bleach and toilet bowl cleaner.
An employee was cutting a heat exchanger with high-pressure water. The hose broke and the water cut a tendon in the employee’s knee.
While painting was being done by a contractor, an employee working in the assembly area had an allergic reaction to the latex floor paint. The employee was hospitalized.

At about 2:30 p.m. on November 16, 2021, an employee was checking the sight glass for a liquid level on an ammonia refrigeration system. The sight glass broke, and liquid ammonia sprayed out of the opening onto the employee’s face, chest, and throat area, resulting in chemical burns.
An employee was cleaning a paint sprayer when a substance from the paint sprayer was injected into his left hand resulting in inflammation, infection, and hospitalization.

An employee was operating a high-pressure paint pump, applying wall sealer to a cement wall in a basin at a sewer plant. While unplugging the spray gun, it injected the wall sealer chemical into his left hand. The employee required surgery.
An employee was using a paint sprayer when the spray gun became clogged. The employee went to unscrew the tip and spray the clogged paint out when paint was injected into his right hand.
An employee was performing plumbing services at a residential home when they were splashed in the eyes by an alkaline drain clog remover. The employee sustained chemical burns.

An employee was spreading soda ash on a sulfuric acid spill in a containment area. He later felt tightness in his chest and began coughing. The employee was hospitalized due to exposure to soda ash and sulfuric acid.
An employee was removing bolts from a pipe in an acid plant when residual sulfuric acid sprayed the employee. They sustained chemical burns to the left shoulder.

On September 5, 2024, an employee became pale, shaky, and confused after a work day consisting of pouring concrete for a business driveway. The employee was hospitalized for dehydration and an acute kidney injury.
An employee and coworkers were pulling fiber optic cables through a horizontal duct beneath the road. The employee passed out and was hospitalized overnight.
An employee pulling wire felt a strange pain in his belly. He was hospitalized to determine the source of the severe pain.
An employee suffered renal/kidney failure and severe dehydration while on the job driving a fuel truck, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was dumping trash in the dumpster when he experienced a headache coupled with nausea and cramping. He was taken to the hospital where he received fluids and was kept overnight for observation.
While on his way back to the work office in the passenger seat of a vehicle, an employee suffered dehydration.
After installing a new roof at the Kendall Square community complex, an employee on his way back to the shop started experiencing cramps in the legs and stomach due to dehydration.
An employee was driving home after working on underground plumbing when he started to feel cramping in his legs and fingers. He was hospitalized overnight for dehydration.

An employee was lifting panels from one place to another place, finished the job and then went home. While at home the employee felt pain in his chest. The employee went to the hospital and was admitted with a collapsed lung.
A crew member became nauseous, was throwing up and had cramping in the hand and wrist. This incident occurred while working on a barge. The barge was not docked at the port.
An employee was conducting touch-up work on precast concrete on a worksite and suffered a stroke.
On June 23, 2017, an employee was tying rebar when he developed a blister that became infected, requiring hospitalization.
An employee collapsed due to dehydration.
An employee lost consciousness and suffered a fractured skull at a multi-story apartment building construction site.
An employee was laying sod and spreading grass seed at the construction site. He complained of chest pains and numbness in his arm. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was pulling wire and installing conduit and suffered a heart attack.
An employee was installing insulation and became dizzy. The employee was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee felt ill and was hospitalized with symptoms of dehydration.
An employee suffered a heart attack after excavating concrete, requiring hospitalization.
After completing roofing work, an employee experienced headaches, cramps, and vomiting, requiring hospitalization for kidney failure.

An employee was stripping a wire at a job site when he lacerated his wrist or arm and went to get a bandage out of his truck. He then passed out and hit his head on the truck or ground, sustaining head injuries.
An employee was performing HVAC start-up work when he was found unconscious and was hospitalized for a head injury.
After working, an employee felt sick and was hospitalized due to dehydration.
An employee was picking up trash at a job site and had been working since 12:00 PM. The employee passed out and was hospitalized with dehydration.
Employee was climbing down from a pole after assisting CMP with storm restoration and fell to the ground. He was hospitalized with a heart attack and pneumonia.
While operating a forklift an employee became ill and fell to the ground. He fractured his neck and was hospitalized.
An employee had a heart attack while testing a transformer and removing the lines.

An employee returned from his lunch break and was performing labor which included removing dirt clods from a small trench. The employee was sweating and pale, and stated that his chest was hurting. The employee was hospitalized for a heart attack.
An employee was on his hands and knees laying tile in a client’s bathroom. The friction from the floor caused a blister on his left knee, which became infected, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was on a roof installing new tile and had a heart attack.
An employee had been removing 8 feet of excavation fencing. After taking a break, the employee went into cardiac arrest.
An employee was hospitalized with broken ribs while pulling de-energized conductor wiring.
An employee was operating a fuel-loop maintenance truck. While fueling a bulldozer, he stepped over the fuel hose with his left foot. His right foot twisted and broke at the ankle.
On 7/7/15, an employee began cramping and felt dehydrated. He went back to an office location and the cramping worsened. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was waiting for welders to complete an isolation on a pipe. The employee started cramping and was hospitalized with a muscle injury.
An employee was lifting a 50 lb. pipe fitting elbow with another employee and suffered an abdominal hernia rupture on his right side.

Two employees were manually lifting a power cooling fan (approximately 60 pounds) off a stack of units on a pallet. While lowering a unit on a cart, the injured employee lost grip, or the unit shifted, and the employee suffered a left wrist laceration requiring surgery.
An employee suffered a hernia and was hospitalized.

An employee was bending over to pick up a 10-foot stick of 3/4" electrical metallic tube (EMT) when he felt and heard a pop in his back and experienced a sharp lower back pain. He was hospitalized with a compressed back disc.
An employee was working on pipes under the sun when he experienced hand cramping and was hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee suffered a hernia while climbing a scaffold and was hospitalized.
An employee was installing an overhead electrical conductor when he strained his chest, requiring hospitalization. A pull strap was not used at the time of the incident.
An employee was helping a carpenter put up some concrete forms. He was installing anchor bolts when he started having cramps in his feet, legs, and arms due to dehydration.
An employee was walking down an embankment when his leg gave out. He suffered a torn quadriceps.
An employee was removing an injection bottle from a riser pole using an extended fiberglass pole when he felt a strain in his chest.
An employee turned while carrying a ladder, then felt a severe back pain. The employee was hospitalized, suffering from swelling on a nerve.
An employee was pushing a 3-foot ductile steel pipe into an excavator bucket and felt a pop in his lower back. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee bent down to gather tools and suffered a hernia. The employee had surgery and was hospitalized.
An employee was pulling out pipe from over his head when his left bicep tore.
An employee suffered a back sprain while moving a lid from a septic tank.
An employee was lifting a box from a truck when they felt pain in their lower back.
An employee was removing debris from the ground when they stood up and sustained a hernia.

At about 11:30 a.m. on March 22, 2022, an employee was helping set a precast retaining wall panel in place. While trying to stop the wall from moving, the employee suffered an injury to the right bicep. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was assisting with a door delivery. While lifting the door, the employee injured his back.
An employee was moving concrete debris at a job site when they felt pain in their abdomen from a hernia.
An employee was in a prolonged seated position while wiring a receptacle box. Upon standing up from this position, the employee experienced sharp pain in their back caused by a herniated disc.
An employee was at a worksite when he sustained a back injury and was hospitalized.
An employee was shooting studs with a 30-pound deck gun. As he twisted to reach an area of decking, he suffered a back injury. Later in the afternoon, he was hospitalized.
An employee was using a shovel to dig a hole for a pipe when he suffered a broken vertebra. He was hospitalized.
An employee was crawling in a small attic space when they felt a pop in their back resulting in a lower back injury.
An employee was loading waste materials into a dumpster when he twisted and felt a pop in his back. He sustained a pinched nerve.
An employee was hospitalized after stepping on a L-shaped nail while working on a construction jobsite.
An employee had his hand on the back door when someone opened the front door and the draft caused the back door to open and jammed his finger.
On 5/15/15, an employee was hospitalized after suffering a laceration to the left pinky finger. The employee was conducting maintenance activities at the time.
An employee lacerated his right hand and was hospitalized.
An employee was loading the wooden scaffold system into the truck and got a splinter. The employee removed the splinter. The wound became infected and the employee was hospitalized for treatment.
An employee was attaching a hydraulic coupler and sustained a puncture wound to the left index finger.
An employee was hospitalized for possible infection of lacerations on the left arm that the employee received while attempting to remove debris from an insulation blower.
An employee hurt his finger while using a screwdriver to perform electrical work.
On or about August 26, 2016, an employee was walking on rebar when the tie wire broke causing the rebar to come up and cause a puncture wound.
An employee was removing trash out of the building. As he was dumping the trash from a rubber container into a steel dumpster, his left ring fingertip was smashed and amputated.
An employee was descending a 12-foot column form and came down on a section of rebar that was in his path. The piece of rebar impaled his left upper leg.
An employee was separating two stacks of bridge railing when one slipped and smashed his right little finger, amputating the fingertip.
An employee fell from a ladder while installing a flex duct. On the way down, he put his hand out to brace himself and his right hand came into contact with a metal RC channel, cutting three fingers.
An employee was framing a soffit using screws and a drill when a screw became lodged in his hand, injuring his left index finger.
An employee stepped on an old screw while installing roof fiber boards, puncturing his foot.
An employee was using a drill to install sheet metal beauty rings around ductwork when the employee’s hand slipped and hit the metal duct, lacerating the right index finger.
An employee was climbing onto a flatbed truck to retrieve materials when he hit and lacerated his head on a steel member of the parking garage, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was working on a ladder, installing insulated metal panels, when he lost his balance and grabbed a metal stud to keep himself from falling. The metal lacerated his left-hand fingers, requiring stitches and hospitalization.
An employee was pulling a hose off a dishwasher. When the hose broke free, the employee’s forearm slammed against a piece of glass under the dishwasher, causing a laceration that required sutures.
An employee was climbing a ladder with a sharp bladed tool when it impaled his right knee as he raised his leg to climb.

An employee was loading equipment into the rear storage area of a company truck when the employee’s right elbow struck an inside latch mechanism on the rear storage door. The employee then fainted and fell backward. The employee’s head struck the ground, causing a concussion.
An employee scratched his left eye on a stationary exterior metal panel of an ice machine.
An employee was installing a wooden office door. A splinter from the door impaled the employee’s left hand, causing an infection. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was picking up a piece of glass with a co-worker when the glass slid and cut the employee’s left wrist.
An employee was stepping down from a tensioner machine when barricade material punctured his pelvic area. He was hospitalized.
An employee was installing HVAC in a residential building when a piece of sheet metal lacerated his right wrist. He was hospitalized.
An employee was doing HVAC work in a crawlspace. A piece of ductwork, sticking down, lacerated an artery in his arm.

Two employees were pulling wire through a drop ceiling. The wire got stuck on something in the ceiling, then came loose as one of the employees was pulling on it. The slack caused him to lose his balance, and he grabbed the metal framing of the drop ceiling to avoid falling. The framing lacerated his right index, middle, and ring fingers, damaging a tendon in the middle finger.

At about 9:15 a.m. on May 22, 2023, an employee was using a 5-pound hammer to remove the weld on a pipe support and knock the support lose. The hammer missed the support; the employee’s left index finger struck the support and was lacerated and broken. The fingertip was medically amputated.

An employee was carrying a pressure-treated 2x6 board while plating a foundation. The employee put the board on an anchor bolt when a 3-inch sliver of wood got caught in his hand, resulting in a punctured tendon.

An employee was helping coworkers trying to undo tension on a 1.5 ton come-a-long. The injured employee struck the angle brace that the come-a-long was attached to. The hook of the come-a-long broke free, striking the employee in the lower jaw/face.

An employee was disconnecting an attachment from the boom of an excavator for a transmission crew. When the connecting pin was removed, the 100-pound auger motor he was working on fell and crushed the end of his left pinky finger. He suffered an amputation of the distal end/joint of that finger.

An employee was cutting the blower section of an air unit out. As he was cutting the blower, a section that he was cutting fell off of the frame, which caused the blower wheel to fall to the floor. It landed on his right boot and cut through the steel reinforcement, damaging two of his middle toe tips.
An employee was performing work on a workover rig when a lifting cap came loose from a valve and hit the employee’s hardhat. The employee suffered cuts on the head from the hardhat.
An employee was dismantling a trash chute when he was struck by a 5-pound brick that was stuck in the chute, severely lacerating his forehead and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was helping a three-man crew with a backhoe to lift a walk-behind saw approximately 6 inches and move it forward approximately 3 feet. The employee attached rigging from the walk-behind saw to the backhoe and stood to the side of the forks approximately 4 feet away. As the backhoe operator lifted the saw, the backhoe forks disengaged and struck the employee’s hard hat. The employee was hospitalized for a head injury.

An employee was installing form boards inside a confined space cell. While working inside the cell, a piece of pipe (bell reducer) approximately 7" long, 8" diameter, and weighing 55 pounds fell approximately 35 feet and landed on the employee. The employee suffered a neck fracture and a left hand metacarpal fracture with a complex laceration over the web space.
An employee was breaking down the scaffold system when a bar slipped, knocking his safety helmet off and striking his forehead. The employee was hospitalized for a concussion.
An employee was walking when a plywood board fell from the 18th floor and hit his hard hat. He suffered a head injury.
An employee was using a vertical hammer to pile drive when a steel piece of the hammer came loose and struck his head, lacerating it. He was has hospitalized overnight.
An employee was installing a bracket on top of a pier in a basement. As the top of the bracket was adjusted onto the pier, it bent and slipped off the pier, hitting and injuring the employee’s chest.
While operating a helical machine used to dig holes, an employee was struck by the machine’s stabilizing bar. The employee’s right thumb was amputated.
An employee was using a pneumatic nail gun to nail 2x8 boards together when his right leg bumped the nail gun. The gun then discharged a nail into his right leg, striking his bone.
An employee was dismantling a scaffold at ground level. A scaffold leg component fell over and struck the employee on the thigh, causing a femur fracture.
An employee was removing the housing from a drill rod and putting on the reamer. A pipe wrench slipped off of the pipe and spun around, striking and breaking the employee’s left leg.
An employee was attempting to install a grounding rod. A piece of debris struck him in the eye. The debris was embedded and the injury required surgery.

An employee was installing a pipeline in a trench. The employee coiled tubing on a spool and was attempting to tie in two pipe ends when the pipe slipped and flexed, striking and fracturing the employee’s fibula.

An employee was cutting through a section of piping when it broke loose and struck the employee in the face. The employee suffered fractures in the jaw and mouth, a broken nose, and chipped teeth and was hospitalized.
At about 2:50 p.m. on August 30, 2021, an employee was holding a 2-by-4 in place when a nail from a nail gun struck him in the eye. He was hospitalized.
An employee was handed a paint spray gun to unclog. The gun went off and shot paint into his right hand. He was hospitalized.

An employee was attempting to rig a heat exchanger for removal from the site. A steel shaft was placed across the face of the heat exchanger’s tie bolts. Mechanical jacks were then used to lift the heat exchanger so a pallet jack could be put underneath it. The steel shaft slipped out, causing the heat exchanger to fall forward onto the employee, pinning him under it. The employee sustained fractures to vertebrae, ribs, and an ankle.
An employee was cutting up a pipe pile template. A steel beam rolled and struck the employee’s left leg, breaking their tibia and fibula.

An employee was signaling a forklift to offload material. He told the forklift to stop, got beside the material, and then fell, grabbing onto the tubes on the forklift. The material then fell on him, breaking his foot, his collarbone, and a rib and lacerating his forehead.
An employee was helping to unload patio doors from a forklift. The wind caused the patio doors to lift and fall onto the employee. The employee suffered jaw and ankle fractures.
An employee was moving a steel beam that was on the ground when it rolled, resulting in a leg fracture.
An employee was operating a drill with a 3/8-inch drill bit. The drill bit snapped and struck the employee in his eye, which resulted in hospitalization.

An employee was setting up a hose to be used for dust control. They were standing approximately 15 feet from the inside of the perimeter fence and were approximately 30 feet outside of the demolition area when they were struck by debris (wood, drywall, and insulation) and sustained a fractured neck vertebra that required surgery.

An employee was repairing a handwheel on a gas cylinder when the cylinder valve attached to the handwheel broke, causing the cylinder to release and strike the employee. They sustained fractures to their right ulna and scapula.

An employee was working on a 10" pipe that was pressurized for a pressure test. The employee removed a flat pipe cap and pressure caused the cap to strike the employee resulting in lacerations, fractures, broken teeth, debris in their face and finger, injuries to the neck and clavicle, and a lacerated finger.
An employee was carrying a spool of cable. The spool fell onto the employee’s foot and broke it.
On or about May 18, 2015, an employee became light-headed and "sick" after likely suffering from dehydration on the jobsite. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee coating gas pipe with solvent experienced a burn to the left arm.
An employee become overheated while laying bricks during a construction project at a church.
An employee felt sick while sitting in his crane and showed signs of heat illness. He was hospitalized for severe dehydration.

The employee showed up to work at 6:00 am. At 6:15 am, the employee began sweating profusely. The employee was placed on light duty and worked until approximately 2:30 pm. The employee was admitted to the hospital for dehydration at 7:00 pm.
An employee suffered cramps and was taken to hospital for heat stress symptoms.
An employee that was prepping alongside the curb began to feel ill and was hospitalized for possible heat exhaustion.
After working all morning, an employee began to have cramping and feel ill. The employee later collapsed and was hospitalized for heat-related illness.
An employee had been working in a bucket truck doing overhead electrical line work all day. Later that evening, the employee started feeling ill and was admitted to the hospital for heat exhaustion.
An employee was getting ready to start the kettle motor on the tar kettle. The pipe was not hooked up yet, causing hot tar to burn his face, neck, and arms.
An employee suffered from heat-related illness while digging a hole to find a water leak in a 1-inch service line, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was installing a guardrail along the interstate and suffered heat stroke. The employee became light headed and fell over with cramps and nausea.
An employee was hospitalized after having seizures in a car before moving to the next worksite. The cause may be heat related.
An employee showed signs of heat stress while operating a paver during a heat wave. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was hospitalized for dehydration after performing highway construction.
After working all day, an employee became ill due to heat-related injuries and was hospitalized.

An employee was on a barge, cleaning and cutting out rebar from a concrete trophy. Suffering from dehydration, he became overheated and dizzy and fell. He landed on a steel beam, which struck the left side of his ribcage and caused a pneumothorax.

An employee was applying hot asphalt to material layers. As the employee moved toward a parapet wall to cut a roll of felt, the employee slipped and fell forward. The employee’s hand then entered the mop cart that contained the hot asphalt, causing third degree burns to the right hand and wrist.
An employee experienced dizziness and weakness from possible heat stroke after being exposed to high temperatures generated by a melter.

After using a hose to transfer asphalt from a distributor to a holding tank, an employee was removing the hose when the asphalt splashed him, burning his face, neck, arms, chest, and stomach. He was hospitalized.

An employee was operating a miller machine to pour a concrete mow strip in the center median of the highway. He dismounted the machine complaining of a headache due to the heat/exhaust of the machine. He started having trouble breathing and was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.
On July 8, 2020, an employee began cramping and vomiting at the end of a shift doing concrete work. He was hospitalized, suffering from heat stress.
An employee had been setting long span girders, welding, and adding X-bracing in the gym area. The employee was hospitalized due to heat stress.
An employee started exhibiting signs of heat exhaustion and was hospitalized.
An employee was running an asphalt rake to set the edge of pavement. The employee developed heat stress symptoms and was hospitalized, suffering from heat exhaustion.
On June 21, 2021, an employee developed heat-related dehydration after a full day helping a crew install water services. He was hospitalized.
An employee developed heat-stress-related muscle cramps while doing concrete construction work in the heat.

A roofing employee was installing tile underlayment using a hot asphalt application. The employee slipped and grabbed a bucket of hot tar to gain balance. The hot tar then spilled on the employee, and he fell from a one-story roof onto the bushes below. The employee sustained burns on his arms and back.
An employee was installing rebar when they fainted due to heat and were hospitalized for dehydration.
An employee was making construction wood forms when they lost consciousness. They were hospitalized for heat illness.
An employee was raking dirt behind a skid loader; the operator did not see him and ran him over. He was transported to the hospital.

A materials delivery truck got stuck in mud. Employees planned on using a loader to pull it out. While in the process of hooking the back of the loader to the delivery truck, the loader rolled backwards and pinched the injured employee between the truck and the loader.
An employee was working on a closed I-64 exit ramp at IL Route 177. A vehicle being driven by a site employee struck a nearby roller, which then struck the employee, breaking both legs.
An employee was moving dirt with a skid-steer when it contacted a hard object. The employee’s left leg got caught in the bucket resulting in a facture requiring inpatient hospitalization.
An employee’s right thumb was crushed while he was trying to prevent an excavator from falling.
The injured employee was acting as a spotter for the skid steer operator. The skid steer jumped forward and ran over the spotter’s foot. The employee was hospitalized for a fractured foot.
An employee was moving a pallet jack when it hit and broke his ankle, requiring hospitalization.

Two employees were in a scissor lift approximately 17 to 18 feet high to hang duct work. They had finished hanging a piece when the scissor lift activated, began moving quickly in circles, and overturned. One of the employees was hospitalized with vertebrae, wrist, and ankle fractures. Both employees were tied off in the scissor lift at the time of the incident.
An employee was crushed between a truck and a trailer resulting in a fractured and lacerated arm.

An employee was digging a pole hole inside a construction work zone on a city street when a motorist who had fallen asleep at the wheel drove their car into the work zone and struck the employee. The employee suffered a right leg fracture.

An employee was on the ground directing a telehandler that was placing trusses when the telehandler tipped, pinning her beneath the boom. She suffered a compound fracture in her leg, arterial bleeding, and a spinal injury.

A flagger was trying to instruct a passenger vehicle to stop when the vehicle’s side mirror struck her. She fell to the ground and the truck ran her over, breaking her leg and hip. She was hospitalized.
An employee was struck by a wire reel that was being dragged by a pick-up truck, suffering two fractured legs.

An employee was flagging traffic in a highway work zone. A car struck the employee, who traveled an estimated 90 feet before landing. The employee suffered broken legs and back and head injuries, with multiple lacerations.
An employee was hanging a piece of rubber matting on the right rear corner of a milling machine. The track on the machine ran over her right foot, fracturing it and smashing the toes.
An employee was struck by the tracks of a mini-excavator and sustained a fractured ankle.
An employee was operating a scissor lift using the remote control box. The employee was struck by the lift and his foot was broken. He was hospitalized.
An employee was on a truck picking up road cones when he fell off the back of the truck, suffering a broken ankle and head laceration.

An employee was operating a mini skid steer. As he exited the skid steer, his foot was wedged between the arm and the cab of the skid steer causing him to fall forward and snap his foot. Three toes were degloved and one bone in the foot was dislocated.

An employee was operating a concrete transport vehicle in the company yard. While making a turn, the wet cement shifted causing the vehicle to overturn. The employee was hospitalized with a broken left ankle.
On November 6, 2020, an employee was changing out a flat tire on a truck. The jack gave way while he was under the truck and the vehicle fell on him, breaking his ribs.
An employee was working near a mini excavator and was struck by the excavator’s bucket. The employee sustained a brain bleed.
An employee was removing a wall brace when a telehandler tire caught the employee’s jeans and pulled him down to the concrete floor. The tire then ran over the employee’s left foot and crushed it.
A forklift ran over an employee’s foot as it backed up. The employee suffered a broken ankle.
An employee was riding on a forklift. The employee was pinned between the boom that raised the forks and the forklift itself, suffering a spinal injury.
An employee was finishing concrete on the ground next to a truck tire. The truck moved forward and then stopped; its tire partially rolled onto the employee’s upper leg and broke it.

An employee was operating a trackhoe to assist in the removal of a 6x24 trench box from a lowboy trailer. The employee felt the road start to give way so he set the trench box down. The trackhoe then tipped onto the passenger side, causing the employee to sustain a right femur fracture that required surgery.

On September 28, 2023, an employee was riding on the side of a forklift when he was caught between the truck frame and a steel support column. The employee was hospitalized for fractures to the neck and ankle as well as a head contusion.
An employee was cleaning the tracks of a skid steer from outside the vehicle. The skid steer’s boom moved vertically and pinched the employee against the tracks. His foot was broken.

An employee was operating a concrete buggy when a piece of concrete debris became lodged in the tracks, causing the buggy to come to a sudden stop. The employee was thrown from the buggy and landed on the ground on his left side resulting in a broken arm and two broken ribs.

An employee was retrieving bolts from a cardboard box onsite when he was bitten on his right hand middle finger by a copper head snake that was in the box. The employee had a reaction to the anti-venom and was hospitalized.
An employee’s finger was bitten by a venomous snake while attempting to search for a welding pipe. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was bitten by a rattlesnake.
On 12/2/15, at about 3:30 p.m., two employees got into an altercation. One employee was pushed to the ground and was hospitalized with a shoulder and back sprain/strain.
While doing plumbing work at a resident’s home, the worker was bitten by the home owner’s cat. The worker was admitted into the hospital for treatment when the wound became infected.
An employee was bitten on the right index finger by a poisonous snake and hospitalized.
An employee was rolling up wire while cleaning a site when he was bitten by a spider on his leg, requiring hospitalization.
Two employees were discussing job tasks when they began arguing and shoving one another. One employee pushed the other employee, who fell backwards to the ground, injuring her neck, back, and foot.
Two employees were involved in a physical altercation. One employee was shoved and fell to the ground breaking a leg.
Two employees were involved in an altercation and one employee was cut on the face with a knife.

An employee was being walked off the job site when he was involved in a physical altercation with two other workers and fell to the ground, fracturing his right tibia and fibula. He was hospitalized and had surgery.
At approximately 1:15 PM, was accommodating an empty bucket to sit on it when a snake bit his left hand, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was stabbed in the stomach by a homeless man on the jobsite.
An employee was operating a weed eater cleaning around guard rails when he disturbed a yellow jacket nest and was stung numerous times, suffering an allergic reaction to the stings.
A bee stung an employee in the head as he put on his hard hat. He had an allergic reaction and was hospitalized.
An employee was bitten by a venomous snake while installing dewatering materials.
An employee was bitten by a rattlesnake while pulling grass out of a rock border.
While climbing a ladder to go to the roof, an employee was stung by a bee. The employee had an allergic reaction and was hospitalized.

An employee was helping a crew repair a gate that had fallen off its hinges. A snake was run over by heavy equipment near the gate where the crew was working. The employee tried to remove the snake from the work area and was bit on their right index finger.
On 9/9/2021, an employee was inspecting an array for defects when he was bitten on the leg by a snake.
On November 8, 2021, a wasp stung an employee while she was flagging traffic. She suffered an allergic reaction and was hospitalized.
Two employees were involved in an altercation. One of them was pushed to the concrete ground and suffered a head injury causing a brain bleed. He was hospitalized.
An employee reached down to pick up a rattlesnake that was under construction materials and was bitten on the right index finger. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was stung or bitten by an insect while installing insulation.
A copperhead snake bit an employee’s left arm while the employee was clearing brush.

An employee was working on a hot strip mill when a co-worker approached from behind and pushed in the back of the employee’s left knee, causing it to buckle. The employee fell to the ground and sustained torn ligaments in the left knee.
An employee was washing a company truck at a car wash when a person that had just robbed a liquor store stabbed the employee in the back with a knife. The employee was hospitalized for lacerations.
An employee dropped a bolt which then went into a small hole. The employee reached down to retrieve the bolt and was bitten by an Eastern cottonmouth snake. The employee was hospitalized.
On 6/20/2023, an employee was opening a water faucet valve at a facility when they were stung by a wasp and experienced a severe allergic reaction. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was touching materials with his hands and marking them off the shipment list. As the employee reached down to verify additional material, a rattlesnake came from behind a box and bit their right index finger.
